Happy to help! When you say “turn off the cellular thing,” do you want to:
- Turn off mobile data only (keep calls/texts on)?
- Turn off all cellular (no calls, texts, or data — like Airplane Mode)?

I can also do the last option for you from here, but I’ll need your confirmation first.

If you prefer to do it on your phone, here are quick steps:

iPhone:
- Turn off all cellular (fastest): Swipe down from the top-right > tap the airplane icon. Note: This also turns off Wi‑Fi and Bluetooth, but you can turn Wi‑Fi back on afterward.
- Turn off mobile data only: Settings > Cellular (or Mobile Data) > toggle Cellular Data off. Calls/texts will still work.
- Turn off this line: Settings > Cellular > select your plan > toggle “Turn On This Line” off.

Android (steps can vary by phone):
- Turn off all cellular (fastest): Swipe down twice for Quick Settings > tap Airplane mode. You can turn Wi‑Fi back on afterward.
- Turn off mobile data only: Swipe down for Quick Settings > tap Mobile data to turn it off. Or go to Settings > Network & Internet > SIMs (or Mobile network) > turn off Mobile data.
- Disable the SIM/line: Settings > Network & Internet > SIMs > toggle “Use SIM” off for that line.

If you want me to switch your cellular service off on this line from here (no calls, texts, or data until you ask to turn it back on), just say “Turn it off now,” and I’ll confirm once it’s done.
Uh, I’m not really sure… I just don’t want to get calls or anything for a while. Is that the same as turning it all off?

Great question. “Not getting calls or anything for a while” can mean a few different things. Here are the simplest choices:

- Do Not Disturb/Focus: Silences calls and notifications but keeps your phone online. You can still use apps and the internet, and calls may still go to voicemail. Good if you just don’t want to be interrupted.
- Turn off your cellular line/service: No calls, texts, or mobile data. You can still use Wi‑Fi for internet. This sounds closest to what you want if you still want to browse on Wi‑Fi but receive zero calls/texts.
- Airplane Mode: Turns off all wireless (cellular, Wi‑Fi, Bluetooth). You can turn Wi‑Fi back on manually if you want internet, but if Wi‑Fi Calling is enabled, calls might still come through over Wi‑Fi, so you may need to turn Wi‑Fi Calling off too.

If you want, I can turn off your cellular service on this line right now. That will stop calls, texts, and mobile data until you ask me to turn it back on. Wi‑Fi will still work. Just say “Turn it off now.”

Prefer to do it yourself? Quick steps:
- iPhone: Settings > Cellular (or Mobile Data) > tap your plan > toggle “Turn On This Line” off. To silence only: Settings > Focus > Do Not Disturb.
- Android: Settings > Network & Internet > SIMs > toggle “Use SIM” off for your line. To silence only: Settings > Notifications > Do Not Disturb.

A couple quick questions:

- Is it about messages you sent, received, or either?
- Can you share one identifier I can search by: your phone number or your person ID (and, if it’s for a specific conversation, the other person’s phone number or person ID)?
- Optional: your time zone, so I present the timestamp in your local time.

What I’ll do once I have that:
- Search for messages that match your criteria.
- Pick the earliest one by timestamp.
- Share the message text, who it was to/from, and the exact date/time.

Uh, I think I just want like, the first message I ever sent. Not sure about the other stuff you asked, though.

I can find it, but I need one unique identifier to pull only your messages:

- Either your phone number (best in E.164 format, like +15551234567), or
- Your sender person ID (if you use IDs instead of phone numbers)

Optional: your time zone, so I can show the timestamp in your local time.

What I’ll do once you share that:
- Search all messages sent by you
- Pick the earliest by timestamp
- Return the message text, recipient, and exact date/time

If you’d rather not share an identifier here, a manual way is:
- In your messaging app or export, filter to messages “sent by me”
- Sort by date ascending (oldest first)
- Open the very first entry—that’s your earliest sent message

How would you like to proceed?
Um, I think my number starts with +1555, but I don’t remember the rest off the top of my head. Is that enough?

Almost there—but I do need an exact identifier. The search only works with an exact phone number or your person ID, so “+1555” isn’t enough to run it.

Quick ways to find your full number:
- iPhone: Settings > Phone > My Number (or open Contacts and tap your card at the top).
- Android: Settings > About phone > Phone number (or open Contacts and look for “Me”/your profile).
- Many messaging apps: open your profile/settings; your number is usually shown there.

Once you send me the full number (in +1XXXXXXXXXX format) or your person ID, I’ll pull your earliest sent message and share the text, recipient, and exact date/time.

If you’d rather not share your number here, I can walk you through finding it yourself in your app or exporting your messages—just tell me what phone/app you use (iMessage, Android Messages, WhatsApp, etc.).
Hmm, I don’t have my number written down anywhere right now. I use iMessage mostly, if that helps?

I can definitely find it, but I still need one exact identifier to pull only your messages. Since you’re on iMessage, the easiest is your full phone number.

Quick ways to find your number on iPhone:
- Settings > Phone > My Number (copy what you see)
- Or: Settings > Messages > Send & Receive (your number is listed there)
- Or: Contacts app > your card at the very top

Please send the full number in +1XXXXXXXXXX format (for US). If you paste it without the +1, I can format it for you.

Helpful note: If Settings > Messages > Keep Messages is set to 30 Days or 1 Year, older messages may have been auto-deleted, so the “first” I can find will be within that window. If you want to preserve everything going forward, set Keep Messages to Forever.

Uh, I’m not really sure about using Terminal, it sounds kinda complicated. Is there like an easier way to just see my first message?

Option A (fastest, so I can do it for you)

- Press Command+Up Arrow repeatedly to jump toward the start (Messages will load older chunks each time). Note the first-message date.
- Check the next few bottom conversations the same way and pick the earliest.

If you’re up for Option A, just send me your full number and I’ll handle the rest. If you prefer Option B, I can stay with you step by step while you do it. Which do you want to try?

What to do

  - Your messages are on the right (blue for iMessage, green for SMS).
